questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
An elderly woman, who had two adult children, wished to employ a live-in companion so that she might continue to live in her own home. The woman, however, had only enough income to pay one-half of the companion's $2,000 monthly salary. Learning of their mother's plight, her son and daughter agreed with each other in a signed writing that on the last day of January and each succeeding month during their mother's lifetime, each would give the mother $500. The mother then hired the companion.
The son and daughter made the agreed payments in January, February, and March. In April, however, the son refused to make any payment and notified his sister and mother that he would make no further payments.
Will the mother succeed in an action for $500 brought against the son after April 30?

choices.A: No, because a parent cannot sue her child for breach of a promise for support.
choices.B: No, because the son and daughter intended their payments to their mother to be gifts.
choices.C: Yes, because by making his first three payments, the son confirmed his intent to contract.
choices.D: Yes, because the mother is an intended beneficiary of a contract between the son and daughter.

questions.explanation:
Third-party beneficiaries (i.e., nonparties who benefit from contract)
Type Definition Right to
enforce
Intended
  • Receive direct benefit from contract because contracting parties intended to benefit them
  • E.g., A promises to paint B's house if B promises to pay $500 to C
 Yes
Incidental
  • Receive indirect benefit from contract even though there was no contractual intent to benefit them
  • E.g., A promises to buy B a car manufactured by C
 No

A third-party beneficiary is a nonparty to a contract who receives some benefit from that contract. The third party can enforce the contract if he/she is an intended beneficiary—ie, one whom the contracting parties intended to benefit directly.

Here, the son and daughter entered into the contract to give the mother $500 each month. Although the mother was not a party to that contract, the son and the daughter intended to confer a gift upon the mother—$500 monthly from each child. Therefore, the mother was an intended beneficiary of the contract and will succeed in an enforcement action against the son (Choice D).

(Choice A) There is no rule that a parent cannot sue a child for breach of a promise for support, but such a promise may be unenforceable for another reason—eg, if the promise lacks consideration. Here, however, the son and daughter's exchanged promises were supported by consideration.

(Choice C) The son confirmed his intent to contract when he agreed with the daughter that each would give the mother $500 monthly. Therefore, the first three payments are irrelevant to the son's intent to contract.

📌 Educational Objective

A person who is not a party to a contract may still enforce that contract if he/she is an intended beneficiary—ie, a third party whom the contracting parties intended to benefit directly.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 302 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (intended and incidental beneficiaries).

如果只是顺便得利（比如买别人的商品让某工厂受益）
那是 incidental beneficiary → 不能执行合同

你可能会想：这是不是“父母告子女要赡养费”的道德故事，所以先去找家庭法或“亲属不能互告”的规则。

但考试真正问的是：儿女这份合同有没有把母亲放进“直接受益人”位置，和她是不是父母没有关系。

你要盯的是合同利益流向，不是亲情关系；也不是看她后来有没有真的收了几个月钱。

为什么选 D？

题干写明儿女签书面协议，就是要让母亲每月拿到钱，这个 直接给母亲 $500 的安排说明她是预期受益人，所以她可以向儿子追款。

❌ 概念混淆 | 赠与受益误判

✕ B: 看到 gifts 就乱扣成赠与；书面互约有对价，不是白送。

❌ 事实误判 | 后续付款偷换

✕ C: 把前 3 次付款当成“补强意图”，其实签约当下的受益安排才决定她能不能告。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看合同有没有“直接指向第三人”的付款安排，再分清预期受益人与偶然受益人。

考场速记

记住一句：“直接受益能告，顺带得利不能告。” 看到合同写着“专门给某人钱”，先想 intended beneficiary，再决定能不能起诉。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A flour manufacturer contracted to deliver to a baker her flour requirements for a one-year period. Before delivery of the first scheduled installment, the flour manufacturer sold its business and assigned all of its sale contracts to a reputable and longtime flour wholesaler. The flour manufacturer informed the baker of this transaction.
When the flour wholesaler tendered the first installment to the baker in compliance with the manufacturer-baker contract, the baker refused to accept the goods.
Which of the following arguments, if any, legally support(s) the baker's rejection of the goods?

choices.A: Duties under an executory bilateral contract are assumable only by an express promise to perform on the part of the delegatee, and language of "assignment" in the transfer for value of a bilateral sale-of-goods contract effects only a transfer of rights, not a delegation of duties.
choices.B: Executory requirements contracts are nonassignable.
choices.C: Executory requirements contracts are nonassignable, duties under an executory bilateral contract are assumable only by an express promise to perform on the part of the delegatee, and language of "assignment" in the transfer for value of a bilateral sale-of-goods contract effects only a transfer of rights, not a delegation of duties.
choices.D: No argument legally supports the baker's rejection of the goods.

Contract provisions prohibiting assignments/delegations
Type of

duties
None N/A Allowed
Specific Assignment of rights & delegation of
duties		 Barred
Assignment of rights only Barred Allowed
Delegation of duties only Allowed Barred
General Assignment of "the contract"

Unless stated otherwise, bilateral contracts for the sale of goods can be assigned in their entirety, and this will be construed as an assignment of rights and a delegation of duties to a nonparty (ie, delegatee). Such assignments are generally valid, even for an executory requirements contract—ie, an uncompleted contract for the sale of as many goods as the buyer needs during a specified period (Choice B). The delegatee's acceptance of the assignment constitutes a promise to perform the duties, and the promisee must accept that performance.

Here, the flour manufacturer assigned the baker's requirements contract to the flour wholesaler (delegatee), and the baker refused to accept the wholesaler's first installment of flour. However, this general language of "assignment" operates as a transfer of rights and a delegation of duties. The wholesaler's acceptance of that assignment is a promise to perform—ie, to sell the baker as much flour as she needs for one year (Choices A & C). Therefore, no argument legally supports the baker's rejection of the goods.

📌 Educational Objective

The assignment of an entire contract is construed as an assignment of rights and a delegation of duties to a nonparty (ie, delegatee). The delegatee's acceptance of the assignment constitutes a promise to perform the delegator's duties, and the promisee must accept that performance.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-210 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (explaining that a general assignment is an assignment of rights and a delegation of duties).

MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Third-Party Rights - Assignment of rights

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：整体转让合同（assignment of the contract）在买卖合同里通常会同时带来权利转让（assignment of rights）和义务委派（delegation of duties），所以买方一般不能因为“换了履行人”就拒收。

三秒认题路径：

整体转让 → 权利+义务 → 委派有效 → 履行人已承诺 → 不能拒收

核心法律规则

买卖合同（sale of goods contract）没有特别禁止时，可以被整体转让；这在考场上通常表示：原合同的权利（rights）转给新受让人，义务（duties）也一并委派给新履行人。

委派人（delegatee）一旦接受转让，就等于承诺履行原卖方的供货义务；所以买方要接收这份履行，不能只因为“不是原来的卖家”就拒绝。

真正会卡死买方主张的，是题干里这种一般性 assignment语言：它不是“只转权利、不转义务”，而是默认两者一起走。

核心判例： U.C.C. § 2-210 — 一般性转让通常被理解为权利转让 + 义务委派，而不是只转一半。

思维导图

原卖方
flour manufacturer
→
整体转让
assignment of the contract
→
新履行人
wholesaler / delegatee
→
买方必须接受履行
promisee accepts performance
先看：题干是不是“整体转让合同”而不是单独转权利？
是：默认权利转让 + 义务委派一起生效。
委派人接受：等于承诺按原合同供货。
卡点：不能因为“换人履行”就拒收
结论：选 D，没有法律理由支持拒收。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：题目写了 assignment，是不是只转了权利，卖方的供货义务还在原公司身上？

但考试真正问的是：在买卖合同里，整体转让通常默认连义务一起委派出去；新受让人已经承诺履行，买方不能因为“不是原供应商”就拒收。

司法考试看的是「合同法律上谁来履行」，而不是「买方主观上愿不愿意继续跟这家公司做生意」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干是sale of goods contract的整体转让；按规则会同时带来权利转让和义务委派，所以新批发商可以履行，买方没有拒收依据。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把assignment误当成只转权利了。

❌ 事实误判 | 非转让误读

✕ B: 说 requirements contract 一概不能转，太绝对了。

❌ 法律适用 | 例外搬错场景

✕ C: 把两套规则硬拼起来，还是错在默认拒绝转让。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认出是整体转让，再直接套“权利+义务一起走”，不要被“换了履行人”带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：合同整体转让，默认不是只转钱权，而是权利转让 + 义务委派一起上场；买方想拒收，先看有没有明确禁止或真正不能履行。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A seller borrowed $5,000 from a bank. Soon thereafter the seller filed for bankruptcy, having paid nothing on his debt to the bank.
Five years after the debt had been discharged in bankruptcy, the seller contracted to sell certain goods to a buyer for $5,000. The contract provided that the buyer would pay the $5,000 to the bank. The only debt that the seller ever owed the bank is the $5,000 debt that was discharged in bankruptcy. The seller delivered the goods to the buyer, who accepted them.
If the bank becomes aware of the contract between the seller and the buyer, and the buyer refuses to pay anything to the bank, is the bank likely to succeed in an action against the buyer for $5,000?

choices.A: No, because the buyer's promise to pay the bank was not supported by consideration.
choices.B: No, because the seller's debt was discharged in bankruptcy.
choices.C: Yes, because no consideration is required to support a promise to pay a debt that has been discharged in bankruptcy.
choices.D: Yes, because the bank was an intended beneficiary of the contract between the buyer and the seller.

questions.explanation:
Third-party beneficiaries
Nonparties who benefit from contract

Intended beneficiaries

  • Receive direct benefit because parties intended to benefit them
  • Eg, A promises to paint B's house if B promises to pay $500 to C

Incidental beneficiaries

  • Receive indirect benefit even though parties did not intend to benefit them
  • Eg, A promises to buy B a car manufactured by C
Right to enforce contract
No right to enforce contract

A third-party beneficiary is a nonparty to a contract who receives some advantage or benefit from that contract. If the contracting parties intended for the contract to benefit the third party, the third party is an intended beneficiary with enforceable rights under the contract. That right vests when the beneficiary:

  • detrimentally relies on the rights created
  • manifests assent to the contract at one party's request or
  • files a lawsuit to enforce the contract.

Once this occurs, the original contracting parties are bound to perform the contract.

Here, the bank was an intended third-party beneficiary of the buyer-seller contract because the seller agreed to sell the buyer goods in exchange for the buyer paying the bank $5,000. The bank's right to enforce the buyer-seller contract will vest once the bank files a lawsuit to enforce it. Therefore, the bank will likely succeed in an action against the buyer for $5,000.

(Choice A) The buyer's promise to pay the bank was supported by consideration since the buyer agreed to pay the bank $5,000 in exchange for the seller's goods.

(Choice B) The fact that the seller's debt to the bank was discharged in bankruptcy is irrelevant because an intended beneficiary can be a creditor or a donee beneficiary. A creditor beneficiary can recover to satisfy a debt. A donee beneficiary can recover to receive a gift. Therefore, the bank is likely an intended donee beneficiary.

(Choice C) Although no consideration is required to support a promise to pay a debt discharged in bankruptcy, this is not a reason for the bank to succeed. Instead, the bank will succeed because it is an intended beneficiary.

📌 Educational Objective

Intended third-party beneficiaries receive a direct benefit from a contract because the contracting parties intended to benefit them. They have the right to file a lawsuit to enforce the contract.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 302 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (intended and incidental beneficiaries).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 304 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (duties owed to intended beneficiaries).

如果银行知晓了卖方与买方之间的合同，而买方拒绝向银行支付任何款项，那么银行对买方提起诉讼，要求其支付5,000美元，是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为买方向银行付款的承诺没有对价支持。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为卖方的债务已在破产中被免除。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为支付已在破产中被免除的债务的承诺，无需对价支持。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Third-Party Rights - Vesting of Beneficiary's Rights

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：第三人受益人（third-party beneficiary）什么时候能直接起诉合同当事人，尤其是受益人权利何时 vest（固定下来）。

三秒认题路径：

约定替银行收钱 → 银行得直接利益 → 当事人想让它受益 → 权利已固定 → 银行可起诉

核心法律规则

第三人受益人（third-party beneficiary）是合同外的人，但合同是为了让他直接得利。若缔约双方 intended beneficiary（有意受益人），考场意思：他不是“顺便沾光”的人，而是可以直接拿合同来维权的人。

有意受益人（intended beneficiary）可以起诉强制履行；附带受益人（incidental beneficiary）不行。受益人权利通常在三种情形下 vest：明示表示接受、按对方请求表示同意，或 files a lawsuit（提起诉讼）；考场意思：一旦固定，原合同当事人就不能再随便把这个利益收回去。

核心规则： Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§ 302, 304 - 只要合同就是要把钱付给第三人，这个人通常就是有意受益人，能直接告违约方。

思维导图

卖方 与买方订约
→
买方 承诺把价款付给银行
→
银行 直接受益人
→
结果 可直接起诉买方
这笔合同是不是专门让银行拿到钱？
是卖方卖货，买方把 $5,000 直接付给银行，银行不是路过沾光。
规则这叫 intended beneficiary，不是 incidental beneficiary。
卡死点银行一旦提诉，权利就已固定，能直接向买方追钱。
“破产债务已注销”不是挡箭牌；本题看的是合同有没有把银行写成直接受益人。
答案选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：卖方对银行的旧债已经在破产里清掉了，所以银行不能再要钱。

但考试真正问的是：这次买卖合同是不是专门把付款利益给银行，而不是旧债还在不在。这题看的是合同受益关系，不是旧债复活。

另一个坑是把“需要对价”想成银行和买方之间必须另有交换；其实买方拿到卖方货物，卖方要求把价款付给银行，这就足够支撑合同结构。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干写明买方要把 $5,000 直接付给银行，这说明银行是合同要保护的直接受益人，所以银行可以起诉买方收钱。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把买方对卖方的交换看成 no consideration，其实对价就在货物和付款安排里。

❌ 事实误判 | 旧债复活误判

✕ B: 盯着破产旧债不放，漏看这次合同已把银行写成受益人。

❌ 法律适用 | 对价要件错位

✕ C: 把“无需对价”当成胜诉理由，真正理由是银行属于有意受益人。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看合同是不是“专门替第三人收钱”，再判断这个人是不是有意受益人。

考场速记

记住一句：谁被合同直接点名受益，谁通常就是有意受益人。本题一看“直接付给银行”，就别再绕破产旧债。

如果题目转成中间上诉，再记口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，对应 injunction、certification、class action 等法定例外。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A sugar distributor contracted to deliver to a bakery its sugar requirements for a one-year period. Before delivery of the first scheduled installment, the sugar distributor sold its business and assigned all of its sale contracts to a reputable and longtime sugar retailer. The sugar distributor informed the bakery of this transaction.
The bakery accepted the sugar retailer's delivery of the first installment under the distributor-bakery contract, but the bakery paid the contract price for that installment to the distributor and refused to pay anything to the retailer.
In an action by the retailer against the bakery for the contractual amount of the first installment, which of the following, if any, will be an effective defense for the bakery?

choices.A: The bakery had not expressly agreed to accept the sugar retailer as its sugar supplier.
choices.B: The bakery had not expressly agreed to accept the sugar retailer as its sugar supplier, and the sugar distributor remained obligated to the bakery even though it had assigned the contract to the sugar retailer.
choices.C: The bakery's payment of the contractual installment to the sugar distributor discharged its obligation.
choices.D: No defense will be effective for the bakery.

Contract provisions prohibiting assignments/delegations
Type of
provision		 Explicit prohibitions Assignment of

None N/A Allowed

Assignment of rights only Barred Allowed
Delegation of duties only Allowed Barred
General Assignment of "the contract"

Either party to a contract can assign its rights or delegate its duties to a nonparty (ie, delegatee). A general assignment of the entire contract will be construed as both an assignment of rights AND a delegation of duties. For example, a seller's general assignment of an entire contract gives the delegatee the right to receive payment directly from the buyer provided that the delegatee delivers the goods.

Here, the sugar distributor assigned the bakery's requirements contract to the sugar retailer, which operated as an assignment of rights and a delegation of duties. The retailer then had a right to receive payment directly from the bakery since the retailer delivered the first installment of sugar to it. Therefore, the bakery's payment to the distributor did not discharge its obligation to pay the retailer (Choice C).

(Choices A & B) Unless the contract states otherwise, contractual duties can be delegated without the promisee's express consent. Therefore, the bakery must accept the sugar retailer as its sugar supplier even though she did not expressly agree to do so. And though the sugar distributor remains liable to the bakery if the retailer fails to perform, the retailer did perform by delivering the first installment.

📌 Educational Objective

A general assignment of an entire contract will be construed as both an assignment of rights and a delegation of duties to a nonparty (ie, delegatee). For example, a seller's assignment of an entire contract gives the delegatee the duty to deliver the goods and the right to receive payment directly from the buyer.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-210 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (explaining that a general assignment is an assignment of rights and a delegation of duties).

MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Third-Party Rights - Assignment of rights

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：整个合同的一般转让（general assignment of the contract）会同时带来权利转让（assignment of rights）和义务转移（delegation of duties），所以受让人履行后就能向买方直接收款。

三秒认题路径：

整合同转让 → 双重效果 → 受让人履约 → 买方付款对象变了 → 原付款不免责

核心法律规则

先抓规则，再看这题怎么落

在合同法里，一方通常可以把权利（rights）让给第三人，也可以把义务（duties）委托第三人去履行；general assignment 考场意思：不是只换收款人，而是连“谁来干活”一起换掉。

所以如果原合同被整体转让，受让人既拿到收款权，也接手交货义务；只要受让人已经履行，买方就要把该期货款付给受让人。

原债务人通常仍对买方承担兜底责任，但这只影响买方能否追原卖方，不会让买方把已经该付给受让人的钱继续付给旧卖方。

核心判例： U.C.C. § 2-210 — 说明“整体转让合同”通常会同时构成权利转让和义务转移，因此受让人可直接向买方收款。

思维导图

先看：这是不是整个合同的转让？
是整体转让 = assignment of rights + delegation of duties
接着看受让人有没有履行首批交货？
已履行 → 买方付款对象变成受让人，不是旧分销商
最后卡死点买方把钱付给旧分销商，能不能免责？
不能。旧付款只是在“付错人”，不等于债务消灭。
结论受让人可以向买方追首期货款 → 选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：买方没有明确同意换供应商，所以它还能继续把钱付给原来的分销商。

但考试真正问的是：整体合同转让后，谁已经成了该期的收款权人；这里看的是受让人已交货，原付款不再消灭对受让人的债务。

司法考试看的是「法律关系上该付给谁」，而不是「买方主观上是不是以为旧卖方还在」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的assigned all of its sale contracts说明是整体合同转让；受让人已交首批货，所以该期货款应付给受让人，付给旧分销商不能免责。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“必须明示同意”当成转让门槛了。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间上诉理由误判

✕ B: 你抓住了旧卖方仍负担保责任，却忽略买方已要向受让人付款。

❌ 事实误判 | 付款对象偷换

✕ C: 只看见“付给了旧分销商”，没看见这笔钱付错人了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先识别是不是整体合同转让，再看受让人是否已履行，最后判断买方该向谁付款。

考场速记

记住一句：整个合同一转让，权利义务一起走；受让人一旦履行，买方就该向受让人付款，别再把钱打给旧合同方。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A landowner advertised a proposed sale of standing timber on a choice 2,000-acre tract. A construction enterprise offered a fair price for the timber rights in question. The landowner accepted the offer and the parties entered into a written contract.
Later, without legal excuse and over the landowner's strong objection, the construction enterprise repudiated the contract before commencing performance. The landowner could not afford to hire a lawyer and take legal action, and he made no attempt to assign any cause of action he might have had against the construction enterprise.
If the construction enterprise is sued for breach of the contract by the landowner's next-door neighbor, whose view of a nearby lake is obscured by the standing timber, will the neighbor prevail?

choices.A: No, because the neighbor is a maintainer of nuisance litigation.
choices.B: No, because the neighbor is only an incidental beneficiary, if any, of the contract.
choices.C: Yes, because the neighbor is a surrogate for the landowner in view of his inability to enforce the contract.
choices.D: Yes, because the neighbor is a third-party intended beneficiary of the contract.

questions.explanation:
Third-party beneficiaries

Nonparties who benefit from contract

Intended beneficiaries

  • Receive direct benefit because parties intended to benefit them
  • Eg, A promises to paint B's house if B promises to pay $500 to C
Right to enforce contract

Incidental beneficiaries

  • Receive indirect benefit even though parties did not intend to benefit them
  • Eg, A promises to buy B a car manufactured by C
No right to enforce contract

A third-party beneficiary is a nonparty to a contract who receives some advantage or benefit from that contract. Unlike intended beneficiaries, incidental beneficiaries—ie, those whom the contracting parties did not intend to benefit directly—have no right to sue under the contract.

Here, the neighbor is at most an incidental beneficiary of the contract between the landowner and the construction enterprise since there was no contractual intent to benefit the neighbor (eg, improve the neighbor's view of the lake). As an incidental beneficiary, the neighbor has no right to sue under the contract. Therefore, the neighbor will not prevail in a breach-of-contract suit against the construction enterprise (Choice D).

(Choice A) The neighbor would not be accused of maintaining nuisance litigation (ie, bringing a bad-faith claim to harass someone) since the neighbor presumably believed (incorrectly) that he/she had the right to enforce the contract.

(Choice C) A surrogate is one who acts on behalf of another party. But here, the neighbor has no right under the contract or otherwise to enforce the contract on the landowner's behalf.

📌 Educational Objective

An incidental beneficiary—ie, a nonparty to a contract who receives some advantage or benefit from that contract even though the contracting parties did not intend to benefit him/her—has no right to sue under the contract.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 302 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (intended & incidental beneficiaries).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Third-Party Rights - Intended And Incidental Beneficiaries

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：合同第三方受益人（third-party beneficiary）里，邻居只是顺带受益的 附带受益人（incidental beneficiary），所以不能替合同当事人去起诉违约。

三秒认题路径：

非合同当事人 → 看受益目的 → 无意图受益 → 只是顺带受益 → 不能起诉

核心法律规则

判题只看这条

第三方受益人（third-party beneficiary）必须是合同双方有意要直接惠及的人，考试上才有权按合同起诉。附带受益人（incidental beneficiary）只是“碰巧沾光”，题干里虽然也得利，但合同目的不是为了他，所以 no right to enforce。本题里，伐木合同是土地所有人和施工企业之间的交易，目的是卖木材，不是给邻居清湖景，所以邻居不能告违约。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 302 锁定本题：只有“被意图直接受益”的第三人才能主张合同权利。

思维导图

先问：邻居是不是合同里的直接受益人？
不是直接受益
再问：双方有没有想“专门让他得利”?
没有
卡死点：只是看上去受惠的 附带受益人（incidental beneficiary），effectively reviewable 不适用，这里对应的是“根本没有起诉权”。
结论：邻居不能以合同违约身份起诉，答案选 B。
如果有
才会进入可执行性判断：有权起诉的才叫 意图受益人（intended beneficiary）。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：邻居因为树太高、湖景被挡，确实“受影响”了，所以应该能站出来告。

但考试真正问的是：合同双方有没有为了邻居的利益而订这份合同，而不是邻居有没有实际损失。

这题不是看“他有没有受害”，而是看“合同有没有想直接帮他”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干只说明伐木合同是土地所有人和施工企业之间的交易，邻居最多只是看景顺带得利；没有任何事实表明双方想直接惠及他，所以他没有合同起诉权。

❌ 概念混淆 | 滥套骚扰

✕ A: 把邻居说成 nuisance 诉讼人，偷换成侵权纠纷了。

❌ 法律适用 | 代位错位

✕ C: 看到 landowner 负担不起律师就想用 surrogate 代打，但邻居根本没有代位权限。

❌ 事实误判 | 直接受益偷换

✕ D: 把“邻居可能受益”偷换成“双方就是为了他订约”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓合同目的，再分辨是 意图受益人（intended beneficiary） 还是 附带受益人（incidental beneficiary）。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“想直接帮他，才有权起诉；顺带沾光，不给合同诉权。”

看到第三方受益问题，先问一句：合同双方是不是“把他当目标受益人”，不是的话就直接排除。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A manufacturer of poultry-feed supplements contracted to purchase methylmercaptopropanol (MMP), a key component of its top-selling supplement, from a chemical company. The chemical company agreed to manufacture the MMP and ship it by rail to the manufacturer. The chemical company subsequently contracted with a rail carrier to ship hundreds of products to and from the chemical company's manufacturing facilities. Among the products to be shipped was the MMP. The rail contract required the rail carrier to "ensure quality service to [the chemical company]" by being "responsive to the special needs of [the chemical company] whenever possible."
The rail carrier inexcusably failed to transport sufficient amounts of MMP to the manufacturer. The reduced supply of MMP forced the manufacturer to suffer a significant reduction in the production and inventory of its top-selling supplement. The manufacturer had to transport smaller amounts of the supplement by faster and more expensive methods to satisfy customer demand.
The manufacturer sued the rail carrier to recover the increased freight costs that resulted from the carrier's breach of the rail contract.
Will the manufacturer be likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the manufacturer and the rail carrier were not in privity of contract.
choices.B: No, because the manufacturer received only an incidental benefit under the rail contract.
choices.C: Yes, because the manufacturer had a vested interest in performance of the rail contract.
choices.D: Yes, because the parties intended for the rail contract to directly benefit the manufacturer.

questions.explanation:
Third-party beneficiaries

Nonparties who benefit from contract

Intended beneficiaries

  • Receive direct benefit because parties intended to benefit them
  • Eg, A promises to paint B's house if B promises to pay $500 to C
Right to enforce contract

Incidental beneficiaries

  • Receive indirect benefit even though parties did not intend to benefit them
  • Eg, A promises to buy B a car manufactured by C
No right to enforce contract

A third-party beneficiary is a nonparty to a contract who receives some benefit from the contract. There are two types of beneficiaries: intended and incidental. A beneficiary is intended rather than incidental, as the name suggests, if the contracting parties clearly intended for him/her to benefit from the contract. Courts glean intent from what the parties said in their contract, not what they allegedly meant. And only intended beneficiaries (not incidental ones) can sue to enforce the contract.

Here, the manufacturer benefited from the rail contract since the MMP was among the products to be shipped pursuant to that contract. However, nothing in the contract shows that the parties clearly intended to benefit the manufacturer—eg, had they included a provision that the contract was made for the manufacturer's benefit or that the manufacturer had the right to enforce it. This means that the manufacturer was, at most, an incidental beneficiary of the contract (Choice D). Therefore, it likely will not prevail in its suit against the rail carrier.

(Choice A) Traditionally, the doctrine of privity of contract prevented individuals from enforcing contracts to which they were not a party. But this doctrine has been eroded to allow intended beneficiaries to enforce contracts made for their benefit. Therefore, had the manufacturer been an intended beneficiary of the rail contract, a lack of privity would not have defeated its claim.

(Choice C) An intended beneficiary's rights vest when the beneficiary (1) reasonably and detrimentally relies on the rights created, (2) assents to the contract at a party's request, or (3) sues to enforce the contract.* But here, the manufacturer was an incidental beneficiary, if any, of the rail contract with no rights to vest. Therefore, neither the manufacturer's suit to enforce the contract nor its reliance on the rail company's promises is relevant.

*Once the beneficiary's rights have vested, the contracting parties are bound to perform the contract. Any efforts to terminate or modify the beneficiary's rights after vesting are void unless the beneficiary agrees.

📌 Educational Objective

A third-party beneficiary is intended (as opposed to incidental) if the contracting parties clearly intended for him/her to benefit from the contract. Only intended beneficiaries can sue to enforce the contract.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 302 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (describing intended and incidental beneficiaries).

MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Third-Party Rights - Third-party beneficiaries

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：第三人只是“受益”还不够，必须是合同明确想让他受益的意定第三方受益人（intended beneficiary），才能起诉铁路承运人。

三秒认题路径：

非合同相对人 → 看受益类型 → 看合同文字 → 只是顺带受益 → 不能起诉

核心法律规则

第三方受益人（third-party beneficiary）是合同外的人，但不是所有“沾到好处”的人都能告。关键只看合同双方是否明确想让他受益（clearly intended to benefit），这叫意定受益人（intended beneficiary）；如果只是合同履行中的附带好处，那就是附带受益人（incidental beneficiary），考试意思：只能看热闹，不能拿合同来告。

合同文字（contract language）才是法官抓意图的地方，不是你事后觉得“这人本来就会受影响”。只有意定受益人才有起诉权；附带受益人就算真的亏了，也通常不能直接执行合同。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 302 — 这题的锁门规则就是：先看合同有没有明确把第三人写成受益对象。

思维导图

化学公司 签 MMP 供货合同
→
铁路承运人 负责运输履行
→
乳猪饲料补充剂制造商 只是“顺带受益”
先问：合同有没有明确写“为了制造商利益”？
没有：制造商只是因为 MMP 会被运来才受影响，属于附带受益人 → 不能起诉
有：才可能是意定第三方受益人（intended beneficiary），再谈能否执行合同
再看：合同里有没有“可由制造商执行”或类似文字？
没有：这题就卡死在“只是受益，不是受益人”

考点陷阱

你可能会想：制造商确实因为 MMP 没送到而多花了运费、少卖了产品，看起来“损失很真”。

但考试真正问的是：合同双方有没有把它当成合同受益对象，而不是它后来有没有真的吃亏。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的供应有没有中断」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干只说明制造商因 MMP 运输受影响，但合同没有把它写成受益对象，所以它最多只是incidental benefit，不能拿铁路合同直接起诉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把privity当成绝对门槛，忽略了意定受益人也能告。

❌ 法律适用 | 既得权误判

✕ C: 把vested interest当成起诉门票，但前提得先是意定受益人。

❌ 事实误判 | 明示意图偷换

✕ D: 题干没写合同是“为制造商而订”，你把顺带受益偷换成直接受益。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓合同有没有明确受益意图，再判断第三人是意定还是附带，别被实际损失带跑。

考场速记

记忆口诀：intended beneficiary 才能告，incidental beneficiary 只能看；先找合同文字里的“为了谁”，再决定能不能起诉。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
On May 4, a widow and a car dealership both signed a single document evidencing a contract for the sale by the dealership to the widow, "as a wedding gift for the widow's son, a new luxury sedan, with all available equipment, for $180,000 cash on delivery not later than June 1." On May 5, the widow handed her son a carbon copy of this document. In reliance on the prospective gift, the son on May 20 sold his nearly new sports car to a dealer at a "bargain" price of $50,000 and immediately informed the widow and the dealership that he had done so.
On May 25, however, the widow and the car dealership by mutual agreement rescinded in a signed writing "any and all agreements heretofore made between the undersigned parties for the sale-and-purchase of a new luxury sedan." Later that day, the dealership sold for $190,000 cash to another buyer the only new luxury sedan that it had in stock or could readily obtain elsewhere. On June 1, the son tendered $180,000 in cash to the car dealership and demanded delivery to him "within a reasonable time" of a new luxury sedan with all available equipment.
The dealership rejected the tender and denied any obligation.
If the son sues the dealership for breach of contract, which of the following will the court probably decide?

choices.A: The dealership wins, because it reasonably and prejudicially relied on its contract of mutual rescission with the widow by selling the only readily available new luxury sedan to another buyer.
choices.B: The dealership wins, because the son, if an intended beneficiary at all of the widow-dealership contract, was only a donee beneficiary.
choices.C: The son wins, because his rights as an assignee for value of the May 4 widow-dealership contract cannot be cut off by agreement between the original parties.
choices.D: The son wins, because his rights as a third-party intended beneficiary became vested by his prejudicial reliance in selling his sports car on May 20.

questions.explanation:
Intended third-party beneficiaries' recovery for breach
Type of beneficiary Versus party obligated to pay for benefit Versus party obligated to confer benefit
Donee (recipient of gift) Cannot recover unless detrimental reliance satisfied Can recover if rights vested through:
  • detrimental reliance
  • manifestation of assent OR
  • lawsuit
Creditor (satisfaction of debt) Can recover

A contract formed for the primary purpose of benefitting a third party can be modified or rescinded until the rights of the third party (ie, intended beneficiary) have vested. Vesting occurs when the beneficiary:

  • detrimentally relies on the rights created
  • manifests assent to the contract at one party's request or
  • files a lawsuit to enforce the contract.

Vested rights cannot be modified without the beneficiary's consent, and vesting allows the beneficiary to recover for breach from the party obligated to confer the benefit.

Here, the widow contracted with the dealership to buy a luxury sedan for her son—the intended beneficiary of the contract. On May 20, the son prejudicially (ie, detrimentally) relied on this prospective gift by selling his sports car at a bargain price. The son's rights vested at that time, so the widow and the dealership could not rescind the contract on May 25 without his consent. And because the dealership sold the sedan to another buyer, the son will probably win his breach-of-contract suit.

(Choice A) It was unreasonable for the dealership to rely on its contract of mutual rescission since the son had already informed the dealership about the sale of his sports car in reliance on the prospective gift.

(Choice B) The son was a donee beneficiary because the luxury sedan was a gift. But his vested rights could not be modified without his consent, regardless of whether he was a donee or creditor beneficiary.

(Choice C) Although contract rights can be assigned (ie, transferred) for value, the son was an intended third-party beneficiary (not an assignee) since his gift was the primary purpose of the contract.

📌 Educational Objective

An intended beneficiary's contractual rights vest when the beneficiary (1) detrimentally relies on the rights created, (2) manifests assent to the contract, or (3) sues to enforce it. Once vesting occurs, the contracting parties cannot modify the beneficiary's rights without the beneficiary's consent.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 311 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (variation of a duty to a beneficiary).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Third-Party Rights - Vesting of Beneficiary's Rights

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：第三人受益合同里，受益人一旦因信赖而把权利“锁定”，原合同双方就不能再私下撤销，受益人可以直接告违约。

三秒认题路径：

第三人受益 → 先看是否既得 → 看受益人信赖 → 信赖后能否撤销 → 不能，原告赢

核心法律规则

先抓住这条规则

意定第三人受益人（intended third-party beneficiary）的合同，原则上在受益人权利 既得（vested） 前，原合同双方可以修改或撤销。

但一旦受益人 不利信赖（detrimental reliance）、表示同意，或提起诉讼，权利就“锁死”了。考场意思：这时不是看原合同双方后来想不想改，而是看受益人能不能继续按原约定拿到利益。

本题里，儿子在 5 月 20 日因这份赠与安排卖掉自己的跑车，就是典型的 不利信赖（detrimental reliance）；所以 5 月 25 日父母与车行的私下撤销，已经动不了他的权利。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 311 — 受益人一旦既得，原合同双方不能再不经其同意改掉其权利。

思维导图

先看：儿子是不是第三人受益人？
是 车行合同的目的就是给儿子一辆新车，不是把合同权利卖给他，所以他不是 assignee，而是 intended beneficiary。
再看：他的权利有没有 vest？
触发 5 月 20 日他因预期赠与卖掉跑车，属于 detrimental reliance。
一旦 vested，原合同双方 5 月 25 日私下 rescind 也改不掉他的权利。
结论 车行后来把车卖给别人，只能构成对儿子的 breach；正确答案：D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：车行和 widow 已经签了 mutual rescission，那当然可以把合同撤掉。

但考试真正问的是：儿子的第三人受益权是否已经 既得（vested）；一旦既得，原合同双方就不能再偷偷改掉他的利益。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 5 月 20 日卖掉跑车 是典型 不利信赖（detrimental reliance），让儿子的权利先于 5 月 25 日撤销而既得，所以他能告违约。

❌ 事实误判 | 先后顺序误判

✕ A: 抓着 mutual rescission 不放，忘了先看儿子的权利已先行锁定。

❌ 概念混淆 | 受益人类型误判

✕ B: 把“是赠与”直接等同于“只能算 donee beneficiary”，漏掉既得后仍可直接起诉。

❌ 法律适用 | 转让规则误套

✕ C: 看到可 assigned for value 就套转让法，但本题根本不是 assignment。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是第三人受益还是转让，再盯住“权利是否已因信赖而既得”。

考场速记

记住一句：第三人受益权先既得，双方私改就失效；看到受益人因合同安排先掏钱、先卖车、先换位，就立刻联想 vested rights。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
In exchange for valid and sufficient consideration, a man orally promised his son, who had no car and wanted a minivan, "to pay to anyone from whom you buy a minivan within the next six months the full purchase price thereof." Two months later, the son bought a used minivan on credit from a dealership for $8,000. At the time, the dealership was unaware of the man's earlier promise to the son, but learned of it shortly after the sale.
Can the dealership enforce the man's promise to the son?

choices.A: No, because the dealership was neither identified when the man's promise was made nor aware of it when the minivan-sale was made.
choices.B: No, because the man's promise to the son is unenforceable under the suretyship clause of the statute of frauds.
choices.C: Yes, because the dealership is an intended beneficiary of the contract between the man and the son.
choices.D: Yes, under the doctrine of promissory estoppel.

questions.explanation:
Third-party beneficiaries
(i.e., nonparties who benefit from contract)
Type Definition Right to
enforce
Intended
  • Receive direct benefit from contract because contracting parties intended to benefit them
  • E.g., A promises to paint B's house if B promises to pay $500 to C
 Yes
Incidental
  • Receive indirect benefit from contract even though there was no contractual intent to benefit them
  • E.g., A promises to buy B a car manufactured by C
 No

A third-party beneficiary is a nonparty to a contract who receives an advantage or benefit from the contract. The third party can enforce the contract if the third party is an intended beneficiary (ie, one whom the contracting parties intended to benefit directly). Although unusual, a third party does not need to be named in the contract to be an intended beneficiary or have enforcement rights.

Here, the man promised to pay the full purchase price to "anyone" from whom the son bought a minivan within the next six months. The son bought a minivan from the dealership within that time frame, making the dealership an intended beneficiary of the contract between the man and the son. This is true even though the dealership was neither identified when the man's promise was made nor aware of the promise when the minivan was sold (Choice A). Therefore, the dealership can enforce the man's promise and recover the $8,000 purchase price.

(Choice B) Under the statute of frauds, certain contracts must be in writing. This includes suretyships—ie, contracts in which one party (surety) promises a second party (obligee) that the surety will answer for the debt of a third party (principal). Here, the father's promise was to the son—not the dealership—so the suretyship clause of the statute of frauds does not apply.

(Choice D) An intended beneficiary does not need to rely on the doctrine of promissory estoppel—which allows a party to enforce a promise on which it relied when no valid contract was formed—to enforce its rights.

📌 Educational Objective

A third party who receives some advantage or benefit from a contract can enforce the contract if the third party is an intended beneficiary—even if the third party is not specifically named in the contract.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 302 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (intended and incidental beneficiaries).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 308 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (identification of beneficiaries).

zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为根据statute of frauds（反欺诈法）中的保证条款，该男子对其儿子的承诺是不可强制执行的。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为该经销商是该男子与儿子之间合同的意定受益人。
zh-choices.D: 可以，根据promissory estoppel（禁止反言允诺）原则。

MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Third-Party Rights - Intended And Incidental Beneficiaries

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：第三人虽然不是合同签约方，但如果合同双方就是为了让他直接受益，他就能按 第三方受益人（third-party beneficiary） 起诉。

三秒认题路径：

第三人受益 → 是否直接意图 → 是 intended 还是 incidental → 能否起诉 → 选 Yes

核心法律规则

抓住这条规则就够了

第三方受益人（third-party beneficiary）是合同外的人，但如果合同双方想让他直接受益，他就不是旁观者，而是能主张合同权利的人。

意定受益人（intended beneficiary）的考场意思：合同的利益就是冲着他去的，所以他可以起诉；附带受益人（incidental beneficiary）只是顺带沾光，所以不能起诉。

这题里，男人说的是“付给 anyone”，不是“随便谁都行”；一旦儿子在期限内从这家经销商买车，经销商就被锁定成意定受益人。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 302、§ 308 的思路就是：不必在合同里点名，只要能看出双方要直接惠及该第三人，他就有执行权。

思维导图

男人
承诺付款的人
→
儿子
选择买车的人
→
经销商
买车后直接拿钱
先问：合同利益是不是故意给第三人？
YES：合同写的是“付给买到车的人”，经销商一旦卖出 minivan，就被直接点中。
结论：意定受益人（intended beneficiary），可以起诉拿 8000 美元。
NO：如果只是间接受益，比如供应商跟着沾光，那就是 附带受益人（incidental beneficiary），不能执行合同。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：经销商签约时根本不知道这笔承诺，所以不该有权利。

但考试真正问的是：男人和儿子有没有把“卖车的那个人”当成直接受益对象；答案是有，所以不必提前知道，也不必被写名字。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这题的坑不是“知不知道”，而是“是不是被合同直接指向”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干把受益对象写成 anyone from whom you buy a minivan，这就是直接指向卖车人；经销商一卖出车，就成了意定受益人，可以要求支付车款。

❌ 事实误判 | 未知身份误判

✕ A: 把“没提前知道”当成致命点了。经销商后来卖了车就已被直接指向，neither identified 不是挡箭牌。

❌ 法律适用 | 保证人误套

✕ B: 误把父子间的付款承诺当成替第三人还债的 suretyship。

❌ 概念混淆 | 依赖关系错置

✕ D: 乱搬 promissory estoppel，但这里已经有有效合同，不需要靠信赖补漏洞。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找“谁被直接点名受益”，再分清是 intended 还是 incidental，最后才看对方有没有资格起诉。

考场速记

记忆口诀：intent to benefit = enforce，只是顺便受益就不能告。看到“付给将来买到车的人”这类话，先想第三方受益人，再想能不能起诉。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A computer retail outlet contracted to service a bank's computer equipment for one year at a fixed monthly fee under a contract that was silent as to assignment or delegation by either party. Three months later, the retail outlet sold the service portion of its business to an experienced and well-financed computer service company. The only provision in the agreement between the retail outlet and the computer service company relating to the outlet's contract with the bank stated that the outlet "hereby assigns all of its computer service contracts to the computer service company."
The computer service company performed the monthly maintenance required under the service contract. Its performance was defective, however, and caused damage to the bank's operations.
Whom can the bank sue for damages arising from the computer service company's defective performance?

choices.A: Either the retail outlet or the computer service company, because since each has the right to enforce the bank's performance of its contract with the retail outlet, mutuality of remedy renders either potentially liable for the defective performance.
choices.B: Either the retail outlet or the computer service company, because the bank has not released the outlet and the bank is an intended beneficiary of the outlet's agreement with the computer service company.
choices.C: The computer service company only, because it is a qualified and a financially responsible supplier of computer services.
choices.D: The retail outlet only, because the computer service company made no promises to the bank.

questions.explanation:
Promise's recovery for breach after promisor delegates duties

Versus promisor Versus delegatee
Informal delegation ✓
Contractual delegation ✓ ✓
Contractual delegation
+ release (ie, novation)		 ✓

Contractual duties can be delegated by a party (ie, the promisor) to a nonparty (ie, the delegatee). An assignment of the entire contract will be construed as an assignment of rights and a delegation of duties. But even after a delegation of duties, the promisor remains liable for breach if the delegatee fails to perform—unless the promisee agrees to release the promisor from his/her duties.

Here, the computer retail outlet and the bank entered a service contract that was silent as to assignment or delegation by either party. The retail outlet assigned the entire contract (ie, rights and duties) to a computer service company, but the bank did not release the retail outlet from its duties. So even though the computer service company was qualified and financially responsible, the bank can sue the retail outlet for damages arising from the computer service company's defective performance (Choice C).

When, as here, the promisor delegates his/her duties by forming a separate contract with the delegatee, the promisee of the original contract becomes an intended beneficiary of that separate contract. This allows the promisee to sue the delegatee (in addition to the promisor) in the event of a breach. The bank, as the intended beneficiary of the agreement between the retail outlet and the computer service company, can therefore sue the computer service company for damages—even though it made no promises to the bank (Choice D).

(Choice A) Under the mutuality-of-remedy doctrine, neither party to a contract can obtain specific performance unless that remedy is available to both parties. But this doctrine is irrelevant to determining whom the bank can sue for damages.

📌 Educational Objective

A party to a contract (ie, the promisor) can delegate his/her duties to a nonparty (ie, the delegatee). But even after this occurs, the promisor remains liable for breach if the delegatee fails to perform—unless the promisee agrees to release the promisor from his/her duties.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 318 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that delegation of a contractual duty does not discharge the promisor's liability for breach).

电脑服务公司履行了服务合同所要求的每月维护工作。然而，其履行存在瑕疵，给银行的运营造成了损害。

对于电脑服务公司因瑕疵履行而造成的损害，银行可以向谁起诉要求赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 零售店或电脑服务公司均可，因为既然双方都有权强制银行履行其与零售店的合同，救济的相互性（mutuality of remedy）使得任何一方都可能对瑕疵履行承担责任。
zh-choices.B: 零售店或电脑服务公司均可，因为银行并未免除零售店的责任，并且银行是零售店与电脑服务公司之间协议的意定受益人。
zh-choices.C: 仅电脑服务公司，因为它是一家合格且财务状况良好的电脑服务供应商。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Third-Party Rights - Delegation of duties

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：合同义务转让（delegation of duties）后，原 promisor 还会不会继续对 promisee 承担违约责任，以及 受让人（delegatee） 能不能被 promisee 直接起诉。

三秒认题路径：

先看 delegation → 再看有无 release → 原债务人仍在 → 还能告 delegatee → 选“都能告”

核心法律规则

义务委托（delegation）只是在考场上把履行任务交给别人做，不是自动免责；除非 promisee 明确放人，也就是 release / novation，不然原 promisor 还是要为 delegatee 的违约负责。

整个合同转让（assignment of the entire contract）在考试里通常会被当成“权利转让 + 义务委托”一起看，所以银行既可以抓原来的 retail outlet，也可以抓新的 computer service company。

intended beneficiary 的考场意思：原合同一方和受让人另签的新合同，会把原合同的对方变成这份新合同的受益人，所以他能直接告 delegatee。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 318 锁死本题结论：delegation 不会自动解除 promisor 的违约责任。

思维导图

题干先问：retail outlet 把 服务合同 卖给别人后，银行还能告谁？
第一步看到的是 assignment of the entire contract → 考场上先拆成 权利转让 + 义务委托
第二步问有没有 release / novation？
没有 release → 原 promisor 还在 → 银行仍可告 retail outlet
第三步原 promisor 和 delegatee 另有合同 → 银行成了 intended beneficiary
结论银行可同时告 promisor 和 delegatee → 选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：delegatee 既然更专业、也更有钱，那就应该只告它。

但考试真正问的是：有没有 release。没有 release，原 promisor 还在；而且新合同还会让银行变成 intended beneficiary，所以两边都能追。

司法考试看的是「法律责任链条能不能断掉」，而不是「新公司看起来更靠谱」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干只做了 delegation，没有 release，所以 retail outlet 还要负责；同时银行还是新合同的 intended beneficiary，也能告 computer service company。

❌ 概念混淆 | 救济混同

✕ A: 把 mutuality of remedy 当成赔偿责任规则了。

❌ 法律适用 | 专业性误判

✕ C: qualified 只说明它能履行，不会替代 bank 对原 promisor 的权利。

❌ 事实误判 | 忽略受益人

✕ D: 以为 no promises 就不能被告，漏掉了 intended beneficiary。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“有没有 release”，再顺手检查新合同是否把原债权人变成 beneficiary。

考场速记

记住一句：delegation 只换人做事，不等于换人背锅；想让原 promisor 彻底脱身，必须有 release / novation。

顺手背这个口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 只用于程序例外；本题不是上诉题，别把它带偏。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
Under the terms of a written contract, a contractor agreed to construct a garage for a homeowner for $10,000. Nothing was stated in the parties' negotiations or in the contract about progress payments during the course of the work. After completing 25% of the garage strictly according to the homeowner's specifications, the contractor assigned his rights under the contract to a bank as security for an $8,000 loan. The bank immediately notified the homeowner of the assignment.
The contractor then, without legal excuse, abandoned the job before it was half-complete. The contractor subsequently defaulted on the loan from the bank. The contractor has no assets. It will cost the homeowner at least $8,000 to get the garage finished by another builder.
If the bank sues the homeowner for $8,000, which of the following will the court decide?

choices.A: The bank wins, because the bank as a secured creditor over the contractor is entitled to priority over the homeowner's unsecured claim against the contractor.
choices.B: The bank wins, because the contract was in existence and the contractor was not in breach when the bank gave the homeowner notice of the assignment.
choices.C: The homeowner wins, because her claim against the contractor arose prior to the contractor's default on his loan from the bank.
choices.D: The homeowner wins, because her right to recoupment on account of the contractor's breach is available against the bank as the contractor's assignee.

questions.explanation:
Assignment of contractual rights
Limitations
  • Assignment permitted unless it:
    • materially increases obligor's contractual duties or risks
    • materially reduces obligor's chance of obtaining performance or
    • is void (not merely prohibited) under contract provision
Requirements
  • Present intent to immediately assign right
  • Consideration generally required to make assignment irrevocable
    • Exceptions: promissory estoppel, delivery of document symbolizing assigned right (eg, stock certificate), delivery of written & signed assignment
Assignee's
rights
  • Assumes all of assignor's rights as contract stands at time of assignment, subject to claims/defenses that:
    • accrued before obligor received notice of assignment or
    • stem from assignor's present or future failure to perform
  • Assignor loses rights & therefore cannot enforce contract

A party to a contract is generally free to assign (ie, transfer) its contractual rights to another. The recipient of those rights (assignee) then steps into the shoes of the assigning party (assignor) and assumes all of the assignor's contractual rights to the obligor's performance as they stand at the time of the assignment. However, those rights are subject to any claims or defenses that:

  • accrued before the obligor received notice of the assignment or
  • stem from the assignor's present or future failure to perform (Choice D).

Here, the contractor assigned his contractual rights to the bank—including the right to sue the homeowner for money owed under the contract up to the amount of the bank loan ($8,000). However, the bank's recovery is subject to the homeowner's right to recoup $8,000 for the contractor's subsequent failure to finish the garage. Since this fully offsets the bank's recovery, the court will decide for the homeowner.

(Choice A) The priority of secured and unsecured claims is relevant in bankruptcy proceedings and other situations where claims are paid in order of priority. But here, the bank's secured-creditor status over the contractor does not affect the homeowner's right to offset the bank's recovery.

(Choice C) Had the homeowner's claim been unrelated to the contractor's failure to perform, the timing of the breach and when she received notice of the assignment would affect her ability to prevail. But the time that the contractor defaulted on the bank's loan is irrelevant to her success.

📌 Educational Objective

An assignee assumes all of the assignor's contractual rights that exist at the time of the assignment. However, the assignment is subject to any claims or defenses that (1) the obligor could have raised before receiving notice of the assignment or (2) stem from the assignor's failure to perform.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 336 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (defenses against assignee).

Contracts: Third-Party Rights - Assignment of rights

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

核心法律规则

一眼抓住规则

合同权利一般可以转让；受让人会承接转让人当时的合同权利，但也要一起承受债务人已有的抗辩，以及来自转让人之后未履行的抗辩。受让人（assignee）不是“清洗后版本”，所以转让后如果转让人自己毁约，债务人可以拿这个理由去对付受让人。

这里的关键不是银行先通知了没有，而是承包商后来无正当理由停工，户主因此有抵扣（recoupment）权，可以直接拿来对冲银行想收的款。

核心判例：《Restatement (Second) of Contracts》§336 - 受让人受让到的，是带着既有抗辩的合同权利；转让人后续失约形成的抗辩也能对抗受让人。

思维导图

银行要告户主，先问：户主能不能直接对银行主张“承包商后来违约”的抗辩？
第1层：先看权利是否已转让。这里承包商已把收款权转给银行，所以银行成了受让人。
第2层：再看抗辩从哪里来。
如果抗辩来自转让前已存在的事，户主可以对抗银行。
如果抗辩来自转让人之后不履行，户主也可以对抗银行。
本题卡死点：承包商在转让后又无正当理由弃工，户主的抵扣权直接命中银行。
结论：银行虽拿到收款权，但只能拿到“有瑕疵的权利”，不能把户主的抵扣抗辩抹掉。
答案：D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：银行已经通知户主，承包商又把权利转给了银行，银行就该站在更强的位置。

但考试真正问的是：受让人拿到的是不是“干净权利”；答案不是。这里真正决定输赢的，是承包商转让后的未履约（failure to perform）让户主可以直接对银行主张抵扣。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里承包商在转让后又弃工，户主的recoupment正好能对抗银行这个受让人，所以银行收不到这笔钱。

❌ 概念混淆 | 优先顺位误判

✕ A: 把secured creditor当成能压掉户主抗辩的魔法。

❌ 法律适用 | 通知时点误判

✕ B: 只盯住已通知，就忽略了转让后违约照样能反击受让人。

❌ 事实误判 | 时间顺序偷换

✕ C: 把户主的claim说成要看借款违约时间，偷换了抗辩来源。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“受让人是否吃下转让人后续违约抗辩”，再看能否用抵扣直接冲掉受让人的请求。

考场速记

记住一句话：assignee takes subject to defenses，尤其是转让人之后未履约造成的抵扣。看到“权利转让 + 后续烂尾”，先想：受让人不是白板，户主可以把这笔损失直接扣回去。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A builder borrowed $10,000 from a lender to finance a small construction job under a contract with a homeowner. The builder gave the lender a writing that stated, "Any money I receive from the homeowner will be paid immediately to the lender, regardless of any demands from other creditors." The builder died after completing the job but before the homeowner paid. The lender demanded that the homeowner pay the $10,000 due to the builder directly to the lender. The homeowner refused, saying that he would pay directly to the builder's estate everything that he owed the builder.
Is the lender likely to succeed in an action against the homeowner for $10,000?

choices.A: No, because the builder's death terminated the lender's right to receive payment directly from the homeowner.
choices.B: No, because the writing the builder gave to the lender did not transfer to the lender the right to receive payment from the homeowner.
choices.C: Yes, because the builder had manifested an intent that the homeowner pay the $10,000 directly to the lender.
choices.D: Yes, because the lender is an intended beneficiary of the builder-homeowner contract.

questions.explanation:
Assignment of contractual rights
Limitations
  • Assignment permitted unless it:
    • materially increases obligor's contractual duties or risks
    • materially reduces obligor's chance of obtaining performance or
    • is void (not merely prohibited) under contract provision
Requirements
  • Present intent to immediately assign right
  • Consideration generally required to make assignment irrevocable
    • Exceptions: promissory estoppel, delivery of document symbolizing assigned right (eg, stock certificate), delivery of written & signed assignment
Assignee's
rights
  • Assumes all of assignor's rights as contract stands at time of assignment, subject to claims/defenses that:
    • accrued before obligor received notice of assignment or
    • stem from assignor's present or future failure to perform
  • Assignor loses rights & therefore cannot enforce contract

An assignment is the transfer of rights under a contract to another (ie, assignee). No formalities are needed for an assignment, but there must be a present intent to transfer the rights immediately. A party's promise to pay money received pursuant to a contract to a third party is not an assignment of the party's contractual rights, but a promise of future payment. Therefore, the third party in that situation is not an assignee.

Here, the builder promised to pay the lender the $10,000 the builder received from the homeowner pursuant to the builder-homeowner contract. This promise of future payment was not an assignment and therefore did not transfer to the lender the right to receive payment directly from the homeowner. As a result, the lender is unlikely to succeed in an action against the homeowner for $10,000.

(Choice A) A gratuitous assignment (ie, one that is not supported by consideration) is automatically revoked upon the death, incapacity, or bankruptcy of the assignor. But no valid assignment occurred here, so the builder's death is irrelevant.

(Choice C) Regardless of the builder's subjective intent, the lender was not an assignee and therefore has no right to receive the $10,000 payment directly from the homeowner.

(Choice D) The lender was not an intended beneficiary of the builder-homeowner contract because the contract did not provide that the homeowner would pay the $10,000 directly to the lender.

📌 Educational Objective

A party's promise to pay money received pursuant to a contract to a third party is not an assignment of the party's contractual rights, but a promise of future payment.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 321 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (assignment of future rights).

贷款人对房主提起诉讼，要求其支付10,000美元，是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为建筑商的死亡终止了贷款人直接从房主处收款的权利。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为建筑商给贷款人的书面文件并未将从房主处收款的权利转让给贷款人。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为建筑商已表明意图，希望房主将10,000美元直接支付给贷款人。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为贷款人是建筑商-房主合同的意定受益人。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Third-Party Rights - Assignment of rights

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：把“我收到钱后转给你”误当成了权利转让（assignment）；考试要看的是，债权人有没有被立即转到对方名下。

三秒认题路径：

收到后再给 → 未来付款 → 没有即时转权 → 不是 assignee → 不能告雇主

核心法律规则

权利转让（assignment）要求的是现在就把合同权利转出去，present intent 是核心。只是说“我将来拿到钱后付给你”，考场意思：这更像未来付款承诺（promise of future payment），不是把对雇主的收款权直接转给第三人。

所以，第三人不是受让人（assignee），也就不能直接向原债务人要钱。被让与人（assignor）如果没有把权利真正转走，自己仍是合同上的收款人。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 321 — 这题锁定的就是“未来付款承诺不等于立即转让现有合同权利”。

思维导图

先问：有没有把“对雇主的收款权”现在就转出去？
没有
“我收到后给你” = 未来付款承诺，不是 assignment
结果
第三人不是 assignee
不能直接起诉 homeowner
正确答案：B
如果有 present intent + 立即转权，才可能成立 assignment
本题事实
写的是“收到钱后立即支付”，不是“把收款权转给你”

考点陷阱

你可能会想：builder 明明写了要把钱给 lender，所以 lender 应该能直接向 homeowner 要钱。

但考试真正问的是：这份文字有没有把现有合同权利立即转让出去，而不是只写了将来拿到钱后的付款方向。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干只说 builder 收到 homeowner 的钱后再付给 lender，属于future payment，没有把对 homeowner 的收款权直接转走，所以 lender 不能直接告 homeowner。

❌ 事实误判 | 死亡切断误读

✕ A: 把 builder 的死亡当成关键点，但这里先根本没形成 assignment。

❌ 概念混淆 | 意图转权误认

✕ C: 看到 intended 就冲动选对，但主观想法不等于立即转让权利。

❌ 法律适用 | 第三人受益错套

✕ D: 这是把 lender 说成受益人，可合同根本没约定 homeowner 直接付他。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清“立即转权”还是“未来付款”，只要是后者，就别往 assignment 里套。

考场速记

记住一句：“我收钱后给你”不是 assignment，只有“现在把收款权转给你”才是。看到 third party 想要直接起诉原债务人，先查有没有真正的立即转权。
